methodology:
LAND3 (Terra Santa Propriedades Agrícolas) is the only pure-play Brazilian farmland REIT in the comp set — it was spun off from Terra Santa Agro in 2021 with the explicit objective of being a B3-listed exclusively-rural-real-estate vehicle. All 7 owned farms (39,189 ha = 96,840 acres useful area) are in Mato Grosso and are leased to SLC Agrícola on a 25-year contract. SLC operates the farms and pays LAND3 lease income.

This structure means LAND3's revenue (~R$96.57M TTM) is essentially lease income rather than crop sales. EBITDA margin should be high (real estate REIT structure with low opex, modest D&A on land). Net debt is modest at R$57M (~6% of book equity), making LAND3 lightly leveraged.

The 2-row breakdown sub-tiers the MT acreage by quality:
- Campo Novo do Parecis cluster (2 farms, ~32K acres): premium MT Class-A cotton-soy ground at R$8.5K/acre
- Other 5 farms in northern MT (~65K acres): mid-tier R$7K/acre weighted across Diamantino, Nova Maringá, Nova Mutum, Santa Rita do Trivelato, Tabaporã

FMV anchors are IMEA Mato Grosso 2024-25 land surveys consistent with the rest of the SLC / BrasilAgro Brazilian Cerrado pricing.

Note: LAND3 also leases additional area to SLC beyond owned base (the SLC-managed portfolio includes ~117K ha managed in MT against LAND3's 39K ha owned). The owned base is what's reflected on LAND3's balance sheet and in this analysis.

LAND3 is the landlord side of the SLC operating model — interesting comp pair within the universe. Where SLC's economics depend on commodity prices and operational efficiency, LAND3's economics depend on lease contract structure + underlying MT Cerrado land appreciation.
